cve_summary: A size-validation issue was discovered in opj_j2k_write_sot in lib/openjp2/j2k.c in OpenJPEG 2.2.0. The vulnerability causes an out-of-bounds write, which may lead to remote denial of service (heap-based buffer overflow affecting opj_write_bytes_LE in lib/openjp2/cio.c) or possibly remote code execution. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2017-14152.
commit_message: opj_j2k_write_sot(): fix potential write heap buffer overflow (#991)
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Writes all tile parts of a JPEG 2000 codestream to the specified output stream.

Parameters: 
p_j2k (opj_j2k_t *): Pointer to the JPEG 2000 codec structure.
p_data (OPJ_BYTE *): Pointer to the buffer where the tile data will be written.
p_data_written (OPJ_UINT32 *): Pointer to a variable that will hold the number of bytes written.
p_total_data_size (OPJ_UINT32): Total size of data that can be written.
p_stream (opj_stream_private_t *): Pointer to the output stream for writing data.
p_manager (struct opj_event_mgr *): Pointer to the event manager for handling events.

Returns: 
OPJ_BOOL: Returns OPJ_TRUE if all tile parts are written successfully, otherwise OPJ_FALSE.

Logic: 
The function iterates through the tile parts of the current tile, writing each part to the output stream. It handles the writing of start-of-tile (SOT) and end-of-data (SOD) markers, updates the number of bytes written, and manages the current tile part number. It also supports specific handling for cinema format if applicable.
